Offensive Dominance Leads Seattle U Women’s Soccer to Shut Out Over Montana in Home Opener

Diego Dumlao, Sports Editor
August 21, 2026
Categories:
  • Sports
Diego Dumlao
Junior midfielder Kyla Shuster and fifth-year midfielder U’i Kaaihue celebrate after Kaaihue’s second goal as the rest of the team runs up to join them.
Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 4:40
Instaread

After coming off a two-game road trip where they fell to Kansas State 4-0 and drew against Texas Tech 0-0, Seattle University women’s soccer returned home for the first time this season to take on the University of Montana Aug. 20. The Redhawks added their first tally to the win column, shutting out the Grizzlies 4-0 in dominant fashion. 

In the 32nd minute, senior forward Kailee Wilson got the night started for the Redhawks. After receiving the ball from junior midfielder Kyla Shuster, Wilson was able to create space between her and her defender and get a shot off that drilled the top left corner of the net from well outside the box. Not only was this the first goal of the game, this goal marked the first for Wilson this season, as well as the team’s first goal of the year. 

This was a game of firsts for the Redhawks, with freshman midfielder Vivien Villarreal also recording her first collegiate goal in the 49th minute. Villarreal showed off her speed by beating out the Montana defenders to receive a pass from Shuster in the upper half of the box, chipping it past the keeper into the bottom right corner of the net.

“Our offensive coach was really striving for quick plays, give and goes, and it was just a perfect opportunity,” Villarreal said. “I knew Kyla was going to play me back, we have a really good connection there… it was great” 

From there, it was Seattle U’s game all the way. The Redhawks outshot their opponents 34-6, with two of Montana’s shots coming within the first three minutes of the game. This dominance was partially fueled by the team’s excitement at being back home in front of a crowd of Redhawk fans. Seattle U’s coaching staff reminded the team to play into that excitement and show it on the field, but also learn to control it. 

“It’s a home opener, there’s going to be big emotions, so we gotta play with those emotions, but also relax when we need to relax,” Associate Head Coach Rich Schreiner said. “We were a little too hyped. I think once we calmed down… finding each other’s feet and having more fun, that’s when the goals started flowing.” 

One player that successfully played into that hype was fifth-year midfielder U’i Kaaihue. Kaaihue showed why she was named to the All-WCC Preseason team during this matchup, leading the Redhawks’ scoring efforts, tallying two goals of her own. The first came in the 58th minute, draining it into the top right corner of the goalpost from the left side of the field off a pass from Wilson. The second was the result of a perfectly placed corner kick that found the upper left corner of the net.

“This year we’ve really focused on the team chemistry, and it’s always been on. It was kind of finding that groove, where that relates and goes onto the field,” Kaaihue said about her mindset coming into the game. “I love the style of soccer that we’re playing right now so I’m really excited about this season.” 

Kaaihue is no stranger to success. The two goals from tonight marked her 18th and 19th goals of her career. Last season, the Hawaii native was named to the All-WCC First Team after scoring seven goals, second on the team last season, paired with five assists. Kaaihue also led Salmon Bay FC, a pre-professional team in the USL Women’s League that Kaaihue plays for during the summer, to a USL W National Championship, also being named the MVP for that game. 

“U’i is one of the best players in the We need to play in a way that helps her shine and be her best because she’s one of the best around,” Schreiner said. “She’s a leader. You can see her out there directing our midfield and directing our team.”

This win brings Seattle U’s record to 1-1-1, giving head coach Julie Woodward the first win of her monumental 30th season at the helm for the Redhawks. In 2024, Woodward gained the title of winningest coach in Seattle U history, leading the Redhawks to only two losing seasons in her last 29 years as head coach. 

“In the past, a lot of players have said that she’s like a mom to all of us and it’s so true,” Kaaihue said. “She always comes in with a smile on and she’s a leader, she inspires us every day.” 

The Redhawks remain at Championship Field to continue their four game homestand taking on Simon Fraser Aug. 23, Nevada Aug. 27 and Gonzaga Aug. 30.

About the Contributor
Diego Dumlao, Sports Editor
Diego is a second-year Journalism student from Renton, Washington. He enjoys reporting on all things Seattle sports, especially the Mariners and Seattle U sports. Along with being the Sports and Opinions Editor, Diego is also the host of The Spectator’s official podcast, Cherry Street Chat. Outside of journalism, he likes to stay active by participating in sports such as golf, baseball, tennis and bouldering. Diego also serves as the Affiliate Relations Officer in Seattle U’s United Filipino Club. After he graduates, Diego plans on pursuing a career in sports journalism.
